claims.quote: Total costs for the group came in at $468.6K, up 27% on June.
claims.why: All accounts went from $368,891.06 to $468,600.87: +$99,709.81, +27.0%. 'Total costs' is how this group names the total; no cause is stated.

claims.quote: Food cost rose about $3K, or 4%, on higher patio covers, net of a $1.8K Evergreen credit for product lost when the Fremont walk-in failed.
claims.why: Food cost went from $70,769.07 to $73,874.58: +$3,105.51, +4.4%. Every supplier's deliveries rose with volume (Evergreen before the credit +$3,513.88, produce +$796.72, seafood +$634.91), net of the $1,840 Evergreen credit memo. Volume leaves no single transaction: the cause is spread over ~120 delivery lines.
claims.share_note: A volume cause: the increase is spread across all delivery lines, so no transaction set carries it.

claims.quote: Beverage cost was up $3.1K, driven by the rosé promotion.
claims.why: Beverage went from $29,157.14 to $32,228.86: +$3,071.72, so the amount is right. But the rosé promotion was bought in June (25 cases, $4,375): it is in the prior period and pulls the change down. July's increase is the July 4 keg order ($3,980) and summer volume.

claims.quote: Hourly labor was up $65K, driven by patio season staffing and July 4th overtime.
claims.why: Hourly labor went from $113,257.61 to $178,263.62: +$65,006.01, so the amount is right. July had three biweekly pay dates (7/3, 7/17, 7/31) against two in June; the third run alone is $59,136.33, 91% of the change. Patio staffing and July 4 overtime raised the per-run cost by at most the remaining $5,869.68 (9%).

claims.quote: Payroll taxes & benefits rose $6.2K (30%) because July had three pay dates against two in June.
claims.why: Payroll taxes & benefits went from $20,609.46 to $26,785.05: +$6,175.59, +30.0%. The third pay date's employer taxes are $5,617.95, 91% of the change; the rest is the same per-run lift as wages.

claims.quote: R&M rose $8.1K because of the Fremont walk-in compressor replacement.
claims.why: R&M went from $6,735.42 to $11,800.10: +$5,064.68, not $8.1K (60% too high). $8.1K is the size of the compressor job (replacement $7,450 plus emergency call-out $685), not the variance: June carried the quarterly hood cleaning at all three locations ($4,050), which did not recur.

claims.quote: Utilities came down $1.1K as gas usage eased for the summer.
claims.why: Utilities went from $11,771.42 to $13,142.65: +$1,371.23, up, not down. Gas did fall (-$878.67), but electricity rose more (+$2,274.10) with air conditioning.
Occupancy was $41,250.00 in both months: three fixed rents.

claims.quote: Linen was up $4.1K, but that's timing: Unitex's June invoice for Ballard posted in July instead of June.
claims.why: Linen went from $4,070.00 to $8,190.00: +$4,120.00. Ballard's June invoice ($2,060, memo 'Jun svc - Ballard') was posted on 2 July, so June is one invoice light and July one invoice heavy. Moving it back gives $6,130 in both months: the timing shift explains the whole change, although the one transaction is only half of it.
claims.share_note: A timing shift counts twice: the late invoice is missing from June and extra in July, so it explains 2 x $2,060 = $4,120.

claims.quote: 3PD commissions climbed ~$2.2K after we moved Capitol Hill to DashCart's Premier tier.
claims.why: Third-party delivery went from $8,708.20 to $10,899.92: +$2,191.72. Capitol Hill's two DashCart statements went from $3,245.59 (15%) to $5,402.61 (Premier 25%): +$2,157.02, 98% of the change.

claims.quote: Marketing rose $2.4K on our Restaurant Week listing.
claims.why: Marketing went from $3,410.00 to $5,795.00: +$2,385.00, so the amount is right. The Restaurant Week listing ($2,750) was credited in full on 21 July after Ballard withdrew: net $0. The increase is Lantern Social's summer menu photo shoot ($2,400).

claims.quote: Entertainment & events up about $6K for the July 4th block party in Ballard (band, stage and street permit).
claims.why: Entertainment & events went from $1,800.00 to $7,850.00: +$6,050.00. The July 4 event is three vendors: stage + PA $2,350, band $2,200, street-use permit $1,050 = $5,600, 93% of the change; the rest is a fifth jazz Friday.

non_claims.quote: Sales were strong across all three rooms with patio season in full swing, and covers were up 11%.
non_claims.why: Sales and covers are not ledger accounts.

non_claims.quote: We'll revisit the Premier tier in September once we have two months of order data.
